what: Enable Features (MLI, lot/serial, MUOM, multiple currencies, pricing features, etc.)
notes: MLI before items and before the first inventory transaction. Item pricing import needs Multiple Prices, Quantity Pricing or Multiple Currencies enabled.

notes: Set up subsidiaries before importing any data; the Subsidiary field is required on COA, customer, vendor, employee and contact imports.

method: Currencies: UI (not listed for CSV); rates: Currency Exchange Rates Import
notes: Before any record with a currency amount.

notes: Periods must exist before any dated transaction; periods with transactions cannot be deleted.
Don't import account balances until you are ready to go live.

what: Classifications: departments, classes, locations (and custom segment values)
Other lists items reference: units of measure, price levels, terms, tax setup
notes: Items reference these lists. Design units types before items: an item's units type can't change once assigned (door #21). With Standard Costing, create cost categories before items are saved as Standard.
unverified: Position is dependency logic, not an Oracle-stated sequence.
Not in the Oracle CSV FAQ order.

what: Entities: employees, vendors, partners, customers, contacts
notes: Employees first among entities, because sales rep, supervisor and approver fields reference them. CSV limits: D-128. Carry the legacy key as External ID (D-129).
unverified: Employees-first within this step is dependency logic, not an Oracle-stated sequence.

notes: Oracle lists all item types in one step. Costing method and lot / serial designation are fixed at save (doors #1, #5). CSV limits: D-128. Carry the legacy key as External ID (D-129).
unverified: Components-before-assemblies within this step is dependency logic, not an Oracle-stated sequence.

what: BOMs, then BOM revisions, then the assembly-BOM link
notes: The imports exist; the order between them is dependency logic.
unverified: Position is dependency logic, not an Oracle-stated sequence.

notes: Needs the pricing features from step 0.

method: UI or SDF (roles); access on the employee record
notes: Before UAT and before integration users. Two-factor authentication is mandatory on privileged roles.

what: Opening GL balances as of the cutover period end
method: Enter Opening Balances page, or Journal Entry import (max 10,000 lines per journal)
notes: Exclude balances that the open transactions in steps 13-14 recreate.

what: Open AR invoices, open AP bills, open credits
method: Invoice, Vendor Bill, Credit Memo and Vendor Credit imports
notes: Import invoices before payments; use external IDs to link them. Date them the last day of the period before go-live (partner practice). CSV limits: D-128.
unverified: Dating open AR and AP the last day of the prior period is partner practice (Secondary).

method: Inventory Adjustment import (lot and serial items) or Inventory Worksheet (other active items)
notes: Worksheets exclude lot numbered, serialized and inactive items, and Group Average items cannot use the worksheet. MLI must be on before the first inventory transaction. In OneWorld, initial on-hand can't be entered on the item record; use an inventory adjustment.
unverified: The rule that no inventory transaction can be dated before the MLI enable date was not found on a current Oracle page (door #3).

what: Open POs, SOs, work orders, transfer orders, return authorizations
method: PO, SO, Work Order, Transfer Order and Return Authorization imports
notes: Remaining quantities only. CSV limits: D-128.
unverified: Loading remaining quantities only is partner practice (Secondary).

what: Outstanding bank items for the first reconciliation
method: Checks and deposits dated as of cutover
notes: Reconciliation matches transactions that are in the system.

what: Historical transactions, only if D-023 says so
notes: Oracle advises balances, not full history, for OneWorld.
